## Security Review Summary

I audited all 10 source files in the repository. Two exploitable findings:

### 1. SSRF (HIGH) — `src/routes/preview.js`, `src/policy/outbound.js`, `src/http/client.js`
The `/preview` route fetches an attacker-supplied URL and returns the response body to the caller, gated only by `isAllowed()` which uses `url.startsWith('https://trusted.example.test')`. A raw-string prefix check is **not** a host allowlist and is trivially bypassable:
- **Userinfo bypass**: `https://trusted.example.test@169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` passes `startsWith` but resolves to the metadata host (verified).
- **Subdomain bypass**: `https://trusted.example.test.evil.com/` passes `startsWith` but resolves to an attacker host.

Since the fetched body is reflected back, an attacker can read internal/cloud-metadata endpoints. **Remediation**: parse with `new URL()` and require an exact `hostname`/`protocol`/`port` match.

### 2. Open Redirect (MEDIUM) — `src/routes/continue.js`
`res.redirect(String(req.query.returnTo || '/'))` uses the `returnTo` parameter verbatim with no validation, allowing `returnTo=https://evil.com/phish` to issue a trusted-origin redirect to an attacker site — exploitable for phishing. **Remediation**: restrict to allowlisted relative paths only.

### Reviewed and deliberately NOT reported (decoys / non-exploitable)
- `avatar.js` + `policy/origin.js`: strict exact-origin check (`protocol === 'https:' && hostname === exact && port === ''`) — not bypassable; verified `images.example.test@evil.com` is rejected.
- `commands/thumbnail.js`: uses `spawn` with `shell: false` and single-argv input — no shell, not command injection.
- `config.js`: `trusted.example.test` is a `.test` TLD placeholder, not a hardcoded secret.
- `logging.js`: logs only hostname/path-length from a parsed URL — no dangerous sink.
